key_insight: By leveraging panoramic (full-view) sensing and a view-aligned planning/controller, Fly360 enables reliable obstacle avoidance even when a drone’s movement direction differs from its heading, closing the gap left by narrow field-of-view systems.
problem_solved: Current UAV obstacle-avoidance methods rely on limited field-of-view sensors and fail when the desired motion direction is not aligned with the drone’s heading; Fly360 provides omnidirectional awareness and avoidance tailored to panoramic drones.
method: Capture full 360° visual/scene information with a panoramic sensor rig to remove blind spots.
Build an omnidirectional spatial representation (eg. panoramic occupancy / costmap) expressed in the drone’s view frame to reason about obstacles independent of heading.
Use a view-aligned planning/controller that outputs safe motion commands for arbitrary travel directions, trained and validated in sim/real scenarios to minimize collisions.
impact: Enables safer, more flexible autonomy for drones in cluttered environments by decoupling movement from heading; useful for navigation, inspection, and any application requiring full-spatial situational awareness.
visual_elements: Illustration of a panoramic drone with 360° sensor coverage vs a narrow-FOV drone (before/after comparison).

paper_title: Fly360: Omnidirectional Obstacle Avoidance within Drone View
paper_authors: Xiangkai Zhang, Dizhe Zhang, WenZhuo Cao, Zhaoliang Wan, Yingjie Niu
